newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up on rebound, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up on rebound, mood cautious.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended up on Tuesday on a sharp rally, but analysts said trade was likely to be choppy in the short term overshadowed by possible new government policies to cool the markets.
The foreign currency B share index pushed up 4.73 points or 3.23 percent to 151.07 on turnover of HK$144.4 million, compared with Monday's HK$263.5 million.
"The B index's rally was purely technical, and I expect it to correct in a narrow band in the near future," Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities HK Ltd, said.

On Monday, the B index closed down 4.47 percent after a leading A share firm, the Shenzhen Development Bank, postponed a shareholders' meeting due to a probe into share trading irregularities, analysts said.
"People are nervous about any rebound, thinking it will spur the authorities to crack down on the markets," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
The governmnnt began to dish out policies to rein in stock speculation at the start of May, by which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.

Beijing recently said it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading and increased the share supply with a 30 billion yuan quota for new domestic share issues to dampen volatility.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai exchanges have also suspended trading in a number of A shares in the last two weeks for investigations into possible misconduct.
Diesel concern Changchai Co Ltd was the sharpest gainer in the B share market, adding HK$0.64 or 9.61 percent to HK$7.30.
The domestic currency A share index soared 16.24 points or 3.83 percent to 440.48 on turnover of 6.9 billion yuan, compared with 5.7 billion on Monday.
The Shenzhen bank traded at 37.08 yuan, down 0.72 yuan or 1.90 percent, making it the biggest loser in the A share market.
